subject: Integration recap: VPC endpoints, egress, DNS & mTLS next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mendoza <alex@edgeapps.io>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Integration recap: VPC endpoints, egress, DNS & mTLS next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick written recap from our side so we keep momentum and make sure engineering + procurement have what they need. High-level items we discussed and proposed next steps below.

What we heard from you:
- You want Redwood inference running behind a private network path for production traffic (no public outbound calls from inference nodes).
- Must support static egress (allowlist) for 3rd-party vector DB and analytics endpoints.
- Procurement will need a mutual action plan and network diagram for security review.

Redwood options / recommended approach for EdgeApps:
- Connectivity: AWS PrivateLink (recommended) or VPC Peering for our Private deployment; for Hosted we can provide VPC endpoints and a NAT egress IP range to allowlist.
- IP allowlist & egress: We can publish stable egress IPs for your firewall rules. For Private deployments customers can provide their NAT/egress; for Dedicated we can reserve static outbound IPs.
- DNS: We support private DNS override (split-horizon) so you can route model-serving hostnames to private endpoints. We can also provide suggested CNAMEs.
- Auth: SDK supports API key and mTLS in Private deployments. For Hosted (Redwood-managed) we recommend API keys + customer-managed VPC endpoint. For the strictest environments, we can enable mTLS terminated end-to-end with customer certs.
- SDK/setup: We have an SDK snippet for using mTLS (client cert + key) and alternate auth flows (short-lived JWT). I attached a small arch diagram and a mutual-action-plan template.
- Structured output & tool calling: Our runtime supports function/tool-calling and JSON-schema guarded outputs — we'll provide example prompt/response schemas and a short test harness for you to validate mapping to your backend functions.
- Embeddings & reranking: If you host your vector DB inside the same VPC, the inference nodes will call the vector DB over the private network. If you keep the DB external, we need static egress and allowlist entries for the DB endpoints. Reranker pipelines can be hosted either on our side (with allowlist) or inside your VPC via our private runtime.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) Technical follow-up: 30-min call w/ your infra + our solutions engineer — Karthik is available Tue/Fri mornings PST.
2) Security packet & MAP: Vanessa to share the M.A.P. + architecture diagram (attached) for procurement/security review.
3) Example SDK snippet: Karthik to drop a minimal mTLS + embeddings config and a sample curl call.
4) Procurement kickoff: procurement@edgeapps.io to confirm required PO/contract timeline.

Can you confirm the team that should be on the technical call and whether you prefer PrivateLink or Peering as the first option?

Thanks — I’ll shift to scheduling once you confirm availability.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: redwood-vpc-arch-diagram.pdf, edgeapps-mutual-action-plan.xlsx
From: Alex Mendoza <alex@edgeapps.io>

Cc: procurement@edgeapps.io
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration recap: VPC endpoints, egress, DNS & mTLS next steps

Thanks Vanessa — this is great. A few clarifying items from our infra team: 

- For PrivateLink vs Peering: PrivateLink is preferred because it avoids routing table changes across multiple accounts, but we need to understand certificate handling for mTLS if we go that route.
- mTLS cert rotation: do you support short-lived certs and automated rotation, or will we need to push new certs manually?
- Egress: we host our vector DB in a single AZ and need a stable outbound IP range for allowlisting. Can you confirm the number of IPs and whether we can use a /29?
- DNS: please include the exact A/CNAME suggestions for split-horizon setup in the follow-up.

Also please share a minimal SDK config example for mTLS + embeddings (we want the example to include how the client provides the cert and where the vector DB endpoint is set).

I’ve looped procurement on this email to start the MAP and contract checklist. Procurement: we expect a standard SaaS MSA + an addendum for on-prem/private deployment networking.

Alex
CTO, EdgeApps Inc.
alex@edgeapps.io

Subject: Re: Integration recap: VPC endpoints, egress, DNS & mTLS next steps

Hi Alex —

Quick technical answers to the questions above and a few implementation notes: 

1) mTLS & cert rotation:
- For Redwood Private (customer-managed private deployment) we support customer-provided certs installed on each inference node; rotation can be automated via your cert management system (we surface cert update APIs).
- For Hosted with PrivateLink, we currently terminate mTLS at the customer-configured endpoint and support client certs passed to the PrivateLink endpoint. We also support short-lived JWTs for API calls if you want key rotation without managing certs.

2) Egress IPs & sizing:
- For Dedicated/Hosted we can allocate a small pool of static outbound IPs. Typical footprint for production is a /29 (8 addresses, 5 usable) per region; we can discuss expanding if you need high fan-out.
- If you bring your own NAT (Private deployment) you control egress and no allowlist change is needed on our side.

3) DNS & routing:
- We provide recommended hostnames (e.g., models.redwood.internal -> private IP) and CNAME guidance. For PrivateLink we recommend you use a private hosted zone with the provided service endpoint name.

4) Embeddings & reranker connectivity:
- If your vector DB is in-VPC, performance is best (no public egress). If remote, ensure the DB endpoints are in the egress allowlist and that latency from our nodes to the DB is acceptable.
- Rerankers: we accept a candidate list and run a lightweight scoring step; if you want reranking inside your VPC we can ship the model bundle into your environment as part of Private deployment.

5) Example SDK snippet:
- I’ll attach a small gist in the technical call, but the minimal mTLS flow is: client presents cert+key -> TLS handshake to private endpoint -> short-lived token exchange (optional) -> API call with request-id tracing.

Next step: I can do a 30-min technical deep-dive Monday or Tuesday PST. If you can share your preferred time, I’ll prepare an engineering checklist (firewall rules, hostnames, cert details, expected throughput).

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
